raw_title: BYD’s Fang Cheng Bao Launches Ti 9 With Folding Steering Wheel
title: BYD's Fang Cheng Bao Launches Ti 9 With Folding Steering Wheel
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Fang Cheng Bao’s new flagship SUV could be launched in markets outside China as a Denza model sometime in 2027 Fang Cheng Bao, a premium brand from BYD, has launched a new SUV called Ti 9 in China. Denza does offer select Fang Cheng Bao models under its brand in markets outside China and could be planning the same for the Ti 9 sometime in 2027. Measuring 5,270 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,880 mm high, the Fang Cheng Bao Ti 9 is a full-size SUV. It has a 3,130 mm-long wheelbase. Like every other Fang Cheng Bao SUV model, the exterior is designed to project a tough, masculine image people associate with body-on-frame SUVs. The Ti 9 is based on a unibody platform, though. On the outside, the Fang Cheng Bao Ti 9 flaunts Brilliant Star Ring headlights, 22-inch forged alloy wheels with floating hub caps, Starry Sky door handles, and a split tailgate. Inside, the upright dashboard with vertical outboard AC vents, the high and wide centre console, and the boxy door armrests align with the authentic SUV character of the Ti 9. A 1.1-metre screen across the entire width of the windscreen mimics the Panoramic Vision system seen in BMWs. Also Read: BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme Shatters 500 Kmph Top Speed Barrier; World’s First The highlight of the Fang Cheng Bao Ti 9’s interior is a folding steering wheel, which splits its rim into two sections and stows it in the dashboard when the vehicle is stationary. This helps free up space to, for example, add a tray table mounted via an accessory in the centre console. The driver can also use the extra space simply to rest more easily. All the configurations come with six seats positioned in a 2+2+2 layout. All six seats offer massage, ventilation, heating, and power adjustment functions. Under the hood, there’s a 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engine that produces 115 kW (154 hp) and 225 Nm of torque. It is assisted by two electric motors, one at the front and one at the back. Both motors generate 200 kW (268 hp), but while the front unit develops 315 Nm of torque, the rear unit delivers 360 Nm. A 66.48 kWh LFP battery pack, which can be charged from 10% to 97% via BYD’s Flash Charger in just 9 minutes, powers these motors. Also Read: Kia Carens CNG & Clavis CNG Sales Get Past 6,200 Units Within 2 Months In India The Fang Cheng Bao Ti 9 accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in 4.8 seconds and achieves a top speed of 200 km/h. It can travel 400 kilometres in EV mode, as per the China Light-Duty Vehicle Test Cycle (CLTC). The combined range of the plug-in hybrid full-size SUV is 1,630 kilometres. Prices start at CNY 2,79,900 (approx. Rs. 38.91 lakh) and go up to CNY 3,29,900 (approx. Rs. 45.86 lakh).

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_title: Bajaj Pulsar RS200 Gets More Power, Ride Modes And A New TFT Display
title: Bajaj Pulsar RS200 Gets More Power, Ride Modes And A New TFT Display
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The updated faired motorcycle gets an electronic throttle body, traction control, a Sports Shifter and revised suspension hardware The Bajaj Pulsar RS200 has received a substantial technology and hardware upgrade, bringing it closer to the feature set buyers now expect from a modern performance motorcycle. The changes go beyond a new display, too. Bajaj has introduced an electronic throttle body, multiple ride modes and traction control, while also increasing the engine’s power output. The updated RS200 now produces 25.5 PS, up from the earlier 24.5 PS. It also gets a Sports Shifter, adding another layer to its riding experience. The motorcycle is priced at Rs 1,98,441 (ex-showroom, Delhi). The biggest mechanical change is the introduction of an Electronic Throttle Body (ETB). This enables multiple ride modes, allowing riders to adapt the motorcycle’s response to different riding conditions. Traction control has also been added to help manage wheel slip, particularly when grip levels are limited. The Sports Shifter is another addition to the package. Bajaj has not detailed its operating mechanism or whether it supports clutchless upshifts and downshifts, but its inclusion adds to the RS200’s updated equipment list. The cockpit gets a much-needed refresh with a new 5-inch TFT console replacing the earlier bonded colour LCD unit. The display supports Google Maps mirroring, bringing navigation information directly to the instrument cluster. Also Read: Royal Enfield Posts Highest Ever Quarterly Bike Sales With 3.76 Lakh+ Units Other additions include adjustable levers, a USB Type-C charging port, a hazard switch and Panic Brake Alert. Together, these changes make the RS200’s cockpit considerably more contemporary and practical for everyday use. The hardware package has also been revised. The updated Pulsar RS200 now gets 37mm USD front forks, replacing the earlier telescopic setup, along with a wider 140/70-R17 radial rear tyre. These changes complement the motorcycle’s existing chassis and engine package. The familiar fully faired design remains central to the RS200’s identity. Bajaj has retained the motorcycle’s distinctive styling while concentrating this update on performance, rider assistance and connectivity. Also Read: 5 All-New Adventure Bikes Waiting To Launch From Indian Brands The Bajaj Pulsar RS200 competes with the KTM RC 200, Yamaha R15 V4 and Suzuki Gixxer SF 250, although each offers a slightly different proposition. The KTM RC 200 is the closest rival in terms of its sporty character and fully faired design, while the Yamaha R15 V4 focuses on lightweight handling, track-inspired engineering and fuel efficiency. The Suzuki Gixxer SF 250, meanwhile, offers a larger 249cc engine and a more relaxed approach to sports touring. With the latest update, the RS200 has a stronger technology package, including ride modes, traction control, a TFT display and Google Maps mirroring. This gives it a more comprehensive feature list, particularly against the R15 and RC 200, while its 25.5 PS output also keeps it competitive in the segment.

raw_title: Volkswagen Tengo Compact SUV Production Begins, Derived From Tera
title: Volkswagen Tengo Compact SUV Production Begins, Derived From Tera
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Volkswagen Tengo enters production at Kariega after 2.6 million km of tests as the Tera-derived SUV will make its debut soon The Volkswagen Tengo underwent 2.646 million km of durability trials over 42 weeks before series production commenced at Kariega. The program involved 41 prototypes and subjected the compact SUV to varied road conditions where rough surfaces and inconsistent fuel quality required mechanical revisions. The locally assembled model derives from the Brazilian Tera and will reach South African dealerships in early 2027. Those trials prompted a sturdier rear axle, revised engine calibration for petrol of variable quality and separate exhaust, brake and fuel-tank components. Despite the mechanical changes, the Tengo retains considerable parts commonality: Volkswagen reports that 75 per cent of its part numbers correspond to Polo components. Consequently, the factory can assemble the SUV on the same production line as its established hatchbacks. Volkswagen has selected two petrol engines for the Tengo, a naturally aspirated four-cylinder and a smaller turbocharged three-cylinder. The 1.6 L engine offers both a five-speed manual and a torque-converter automatic, but the 1.0 L TSI is exclusively automatic. Both automatic versions receive six-speed Tiptronic gearboxes, a departure from the seven-speed DSG offered on other Volkswagen models such as the Polo and T-Cross. Volkswagen committed R4 billion to its Kariega operations in 2024, and the Tengo is the first SUV manufactured at the facility in its 75-year history. The new arrival also ends a 16-year gap since the Polo and Polo Vivo entered the production roster in 2010. Notably, about 45 per cent of the SUV components come from domestic suppliers. The plant will supply South Africa and export markets elsewhere on the continent. Despite the shared silhouette, the Tengo has its own front grille, bumpers, headlights and wheel arch mouldings. The roof comes from the Polo, but the functional roof rails and exterior mirrors derive from the Taigo. Even the wheel selection differs, as Volkswagen has designed three 16-inch alternatives and reserved 17-inch rims for the Style. The SUV measures 4.1 metres in length and occupies a position below the T-Cross in South Africa. The right-hand-drive cabin receives a revised dashboard, textured trim and a 10.1-inch touchscreen adapted from the Tera. Volkswagen has also specified a 25 W wireless phone charger, considerably above the 10 W unit in its Brazilian sibling. Higher grades gain digital instruments, a multifunction steering wheel and cloth/artificial-leather upholstery. The Trend and Life variants will arrive first, and the Style grade joins the range later. Safety equipment consists of six airbags, ABS and electronic stability control. Further equipment identified for selected variants comprises adaptive cruise control, autonomous emergency braking, front and rear parking sensors, a rear-view camera and hill start assistance. Volkswagen targets at least four stars in Global NCAP tests. The Tengo will compete against the Toyota Starlet Cross, Suzuki Fronx, Mahindra XUV 3XO and Chery Tiggo Cross in South Africa.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

title: Honda Avancier 4×4 (Fortuner Rival) Breaks Cover With Hybrid Engine
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Honda Avancier gets a 2.0L hybrid system, independent electric AWD and a redesigned three-row cabin ahead of its global market arrival next year The new Honda Avancier made its global debut on November 20, 2026, as a three-row SUV built around a new-generation petrol-electric drivetrain. Its 2.0 L Honda Hybrid system is coupled to DualPower eAWD, and separate electric motors distribute traction between the front and rear axles. The SUV also becomes the first hybrid model to carry therevised Honda H emblem. Thailand, Japan and China are among its intended markets, and Australian deliveries are scheduled for April 2027. The Toyota Fortuner has a ladder-frame chassis, but the Avancier relies on a monocoque body and independent suspension. Honda has placed the hybrid battery beneath the second-row seats, nearer the centre of gravity. The new platform also serves future sedans and SUVs, and its body stiffness has been calibrated to preserve tyre contact under lateral load. Engineers adjust rigidity at individual structural points, and lighter aluminium components help reduce suspension mass. The cabin also benefits from the vehicle architecture. Honda has moved the gear selector to the steering column, which leaves more room around the centre console. Rear occupants receive large armrests, heated and ventilated second-row seats, and an extended panoramic glass roof. The door sills have also been shaped for easier access to the third row. Notably, the Australian RS has two individual seats in each row and consequently accommodates six occupants. The separate rear electric motor eliminates the need for a mechanical propeller shaft between the axles. Its controller distributes torque based on tyre loads, road grip and driver inputs, and it can react almost immediately to changes in traction. The system increases rear-axle assistance at a standstill and employs rear-wheel regenerative deceleration to limit forward pitch. Independently controlled traction intervention also responds to wheel slip at either axle. The hybrid engine works alongside a propulsion motor and a generator, an evolution of the established Honda two-motor petrol-electric architecture. The electric drive motor can propel the vehicle at low and higher speeds, and the petrol engine connects directly to the wheels at sustained highway speeds. Revised intake ports and piston crowns promote faster combustion. Honda has also improved lubrication and thermal management in the front drive unit to reduce mechanical friction. The 15-inch central touchscreen in the Australian version handles infotainment and numerous cabin functions, which also reduces dashboard switchgear. Separately, the 12-speaker Bose audio system supports Dolby Atmos and reproduces overhead sound channels in addition to front, rear and lateral audio. Voice commands can operate the climate controls. Honda also plans MyCabin remote functions that let owners check the parked SUV interior and its surroundings from a smartphone. Software updates will be available over the air. The exterior has narrow multifunction headlights, a substantial grille and a straight shoulder line that extends towards the rear. Flush door handles and a concealed rear wiper preserve the restrained profile, and the rear lamps have angular details near the wheel arches. The SUV also introduces the Motion Management System derived from Honda robotics research to coordinate power delivery and brake response. Honda plans 15 next-generation hybrid models globally by March 2030.

raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Royal Enfield domestic sales rose 4.01 per cent in October 2026 as Hunter 350 gains countered declines for the Classic 350 and Meteor 350 The Hunter 350 supplied the largest year-on-year volume increase in Royal Enfield domestic sales for October 2026. Its dispatches climbed by 4,322 motorcycles to 26,145 units, a rise of 19.80 per cent. The manufacturer sold 1,21,527 motorcycles overall against 1,16,844 in October 2025, which represented a net improvement of 4,683 units or 4.01 per cent. Notably, the additional Hunter volume alone equalled 92.3 per cent of that net increase. The most substantial setback came from the Meteor 350, whose sales fell by 2,652 motorcycles to 12,096 units. The 17.98 per cent reduction was considerably steeper than the 2.53 per cent decline registered by the Classic 350. Nevertheless, the Classic retained first place at 45,396 units and commanded 37.35 per cent of the domestic total. Its share had stood at 39.86 per cent a year earlier, a difference of 2.51 percentage points. The Bullet 350, meanwhile, gained 1,306 units to finish the month at 26,866 motorcycles, an increase of 5.11 per cent. However, the Hunter almost caught the Bullet in the sales rankings. The gap narrowed to merely 721 units from 3,737 in October 2025. The two models together generated 5,628 additional sales, more than enough to offset the combined 3,829-unit decline for the Classic and Meteor. article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Gaadiwaadi.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_summary: Volkswagen has commenced full series production of the Tengo compact SUV at its manufacturing facility in Kariega, South Africa. The first unit is scheduled for a customer in Africa. A sub-4-meter Volkswagen SUV has been confirmed for India as well, arriving in 2027. Volkswagen Tengo shares its MQB-A0 platform with the Tera compact SUV sold in Brazil. The Brazilian Tera, African Tengo and Skoda Kylaq are essentially three regional derivatives of a single joint emerging-market compact SUV program.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

title: BMW R 12 G/S Launched In India At Rs. 25.40 Lakh
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - BMW R 12 G/S debuts in Pro trim In India as the 1,170 cc boxer twin, long suspension travel and off-road equipment are some of the highlights of the enduro BMW Motorrad has priced the R 12 G/S at Rs. 25.40 lakh (ex-showroom) and deliveries have already commenced at authorised dealerships. The motorcycle arrives solely in Pro trim as a completely built-up unit. More significantly, the local version receives the Enduro and Comfort kits as standard, equipment that customers in certain overseas markets select separately. The Enduro kit contributes an 18-inch rear cross-spoke wheel, off-road tyres and footrests intended for better control on loose terrain. Its 20 mm handlebar risers suit an upright posture mainly when the rider stands on the footrests. Protection comes from an engine guard and hand guards and a longer side stand matches the revised chassis dimensions. BMW moved the steering pivot forward and upward relative to other R 12 motorcycles and the tubular-steel rear structure bolts to a bridge-type main frame. Both suspension units are fully adjustable as the front has upside-down forks and the rear relies on a Paralever assembly. The saddle stands 875 mm above the ground and the road-ready mass is 229 kg. The wheelbase measures 1,580 mm. Component Front Rear Specification Wheels 21-inch 18-inch Cross-spoke rims Suspension 45 mm USD fork Paralever monoshock Fully adjustable Suspension Travel 210 mm 200 mm Enduro geometry Disc Brakes Twin 310 mm Single 265 mm ABS Pro The 1,170 cc air- and oil-cooled boxer twin develops 109 hp at 7,000 rpm and 115 Nm at 6,500 rpm. The horizontally opposed cylinders retain the classic boxer layout and a six-speed gearbox transfers output to the rear wheel via a shaft final drive. The engine has a 101 mm bore and a 73 mm stroke and the left-hand exhaust terminates in a raised silencer. Electronic assistance appeals to both road and trail journeys. Rain and Road ride modes suit paved surfaces while the Enduro and Enduro Pro provide separate calibrations for dirt tracks. Dynamic Traction Control can be disabled completely off-road and engine drag torque control separately addresses rear-wheel instability under deceleration. The partially integral ABS Pro also accounts for lean angle in corners and its front brake lever can actuate the front and rear brakes together. Despite its modern electronics, the motorcycle visually recalls the BMW R 80 G/S of 1980. The raised front mudguard, exposed engine and compact fairing follow the proportions of the original road-and-trail machine. The Light White paint, red saddle and period-style decals echo its historic colour scheme. Yet the X-pattern LED headlamp, centrally positioned round instrument and 12 V power outlet reveal the techn beneath the familiar design. Furthermore, two rear attachment loops can secure luggage. The Comfort kit provides Shift Assistant Pro, cruise control, heated grips, Hill Start Control and an adaptive headlamp. Its quickshifter permits clutch-free gear changes in either direction. Separately, BMW provides a three-year, unlimited-kilometre warranty and optional extensions can stretch protection into years four and five.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Cartoq.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

raw_summary: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways ( MoRTH ) has amended Rule 115 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, to revise the validity periods of Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates. The Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, were notified on 13 November 2026 through G.S.R. 991(E). Under the amended rules, PUC certificate validity will depend on the vehicle’s emission standard, category and age. BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles will receive certificates valid for three months. Vehicles complying with BS-IV emission standards will have a validity period of six months.

As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

title: Bharat NCAP Safety Drama: Inside The Shocking Real-World Crash Test Of Indian Car
raw_summary: Toyota South Africa's CEO argues Global NCAP ratings can mislead by testing only base variants. The Corolla Cross and Starlet results illustrate the debate.
summary: Toyota South Africa's CEO argues Global NCAP ratings can mislead by testing only base variants. The Corolla Cross and Starlet results illustrate the debate.
article_paragraphs: Vehicle safety consciousness among Indian automobile buyers has reached unprecedented heights, driven by transparent crash test evaluations under the Bharat New Car Assessment Programme (Bharat NCAP). Verified technical telemetry reported by Cartoq.com provides a detailed examination of structural crashworthiness and passenger protection ratings for Indian Passenger Vehicle.

Under Bharat NCAP protocols, vehicles undergo rigorous offset frontal crash tests at 64 kmph, side mobile deformable barrier impacts at 50 kmph, and stringent pole side-impact evaluations. To secure a coveted 5-star safety rating, a vehicle must achieve high numerical scores in Adult Occupant Protection (AOP) and Child Occupant Protection (COP), while critically demonstrating that the passenger bodyshell remains 'Stable and capable of withstanding further loadings'.

What separates truly crash-resilient vehicles from mere marketing claims is the extensive deployment of advanced high-strength steel (AHSS) and ultra-high-strength hot-stamped steel along the A-pillars, B-pillars, and door sills. Standard fitment of 6 airbags, Electronic Stability Control (ESC), ISOFIX child seat anchorages, and 3-point seatbelts with pre-tensioners across all seating positions has now become the fundamental benchmark for modern Indian buyers.

In real-world highway collisions, vehicles with unstable cabin architectures risk severe footwell intrusion, steering column collapse, and door jamming that traps occupants inside. Indian carmakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra have raised the bar by engineering 5-star crash resilience into their entry and mid-size platforms, compelling global competitors to rapidly upgrade their structural standards.

Our consumer verdict: never compromise on core structural integrity for cosmetic add-ons like ambient lighting or fancy touchscreens. Prioritize vehicles with certified 5-star Bharat NCAP or Global NCAP ratings, verified stable bodyshell integrity, and standard Electronic Stability Program (ESP) to ensure maximum survivability on unpredictable Indian roads.

The India-spec scooters will have chassis and bodywork revisions to suit domestic road conditions. Greater ground clearance and larger underseat compartments are among the changes under consideration. The company could also alter battery configurations and electric motor outputs before production. All three Vietnamese models have hub-mounted motors but their distinct designs serve different requirements. The Evo-derived version is expected to have the lowest price of the three. Its Vietnamese configuration has a 1.5 kWh LFP battery and an optional second unit of the same capacity. A front disc brake, LCD console and 12-inch wheels are part of the equipment list. Its 14-inch wheels sit beneath a family scooter body and a TFT console replaces the basic LCD display. Keyless access and hill-hold assistance are standard on the model as well while its underseat compartment measures 21 litres. The dual-battery arrangement takes four hours and 30 minutes for a full recharge. The Kinet has a sportier exterior and a different motor calibration. It can accelerate from 0 to 50 kmph in less than six seconds in Vietnamese specification. The scooter has a 22-litre underseat compartment and its TFT panel accompanies keyless access. Its battery refill takes nine hours from empty to full despite the extra motor output. The model also rides on 14-inch wheels. title: Honda Rebel 500 Launched In India At Rs. 4.50 Lakh, Bookings Open
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Honda Rebel 500 arrives with a top-spec E-Clutch variant and is powered by a 471 cc parallel-twin engine Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India has announced prices for the locally manufactured Rebel 500. The Standard variant costs Rs. 4,49,900, and the E-Clutch version is priced at Rs. 4,89,900 (ex-showroom, Bengaluru). The Rs. 40,000 premium distinguishes the electronically assisted model from its manual counterpart. Crucially, the difference concerns clutch operation as both motorcycles share the same engine and fundamental mechanical bits. The Rebel 500 derives power from a 471 cc liquid-cooled parallel-twin engine – an established part of Honda’s international cruiser portfolio and it makes 46.2 PS and 43.3 Nm. The two-cylinder configuration appeals to both city journeys and longer motorcycle trips – complemented by the low-slung proportions characteristic of the Rebel family. Honda first presented the motorcycle among ten products unveiled in July 2026. Local manufacture now gives the model a domestic production base ahead of its retail introduction. The E-Clutch mechanism represents the principal technical distinction between the two versions. Electronic clutch control manages engagement at starts, stops and gear changes and thus, riders can operate the gearbox without repeatedly pulling the clutch lever. Importantly, the system retains the manual lever for those who prefer direct clutch control. The Standard version, by comparison, requires the rider to operate the clutch manually. The electronic alternative consequently offers greater convenience in traffic without eliminating manual gear selection. Variant Ex-Showroom Price Rebel 500 Standard Rs. 4,49,900 Rebel 500 E-Clutch Rs. 4,89,900 The design maintains the familiar cruiser finish which is characterised by a low stance and minimal body panels. Visually, Honda has retained the understated proportions of the Rebel family instead of introducing elaborate bodywork or large fairings. The two matte paint finishes complement this restrained appearance. Despite its minimalist appearance, the motorcycle receives a substantial selection of electronic equipment. An LED projector headlamp provides illumination at the front and a TFT instrument console serves as the central information display. Honda RoadSync further introduces smartphone connectivity and turn-by-turn navigation and thus route instructions appear directly on the instrument panel. The digital equipment consequently complements the cruiser character without the need for an additional navigation screen. The safety equipment also extends past the essential braking components. Honda Selectable Torque Control electronically regulates rear-wheel traction when grip deteriorates under acceleration. Separately, the front and rear disc brakes receive dual-channel ABS to help prevent wheel lock under sudden deceleration. These electronic systems operate independently of the clutch mechanism and are available on both versions. Honda has already commenced nationwide reservations at an initial payment of Rs. 5,000. Customers can place orders via the official HMSI website or directly at authorised BigWing dealerships. Retail distribution is exclusive to the BigWing network which handles the manufacturer’s larger capacity motorcycles.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: The Indian passenger vehicle market is witnessing aggressive commercial realignment as major automotive manufacturers and authorized dealership networks push inventory clearance programs. Industry data tracked by Rushlane.com reveals substantial price revisions, exchange incentives, and direct cash discounts aimed at buyers looking for maximum value on high-demand models including Indian Passenger Vehicle.

Historically, November and December present the most lucrative window for automotive buyers in India. Dealerships face stringent fiscal targets and floor-plan interest costs on unsold stock. To prevent carrying inventory into the new calendar year—which triggers an immediate 1-year registration depreciation perception—manufacturers roll out cumulative benefits combining consumer cash discounts, corporate bonuses, and exchange top-ups.

However, savvy buyers must inspect the fine print carefully before finalizing a deal. Dealerships frequently inflate the on-road quotation by adding compulsory accessory packages (Rs 25,000 to Rs 50,000), inflated dealer-level insurance premiums, and arbitrary 'handling or logistics charges'—which have been repeatedly ruled illegal by consumer forums and state transport authorities.

In terms of long-term financial math, purchasing a previous model-year vehicle at a direct cash discount of Rs 1.5 to Rs 2 Lakh easily offsets the nominal 5% to 8% resale value differential if you intend to retain the vehicle for 4 to 6 years. Furthermore, buyers can legally purchase comprehensive motor insurance independently from online aggregators, easily saving an additional Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000 compared to showroom quotes.

Our buyer recommendation: visit multiple authorized dealer showrooms in your city, request an itemized price breakdown excluding optional accessories and handling fees, and negotiate matching dealer discounts during the closing week of the month when sales managers are eager to meet monthly volume quotas.

raw_title: Kia Seltos Attains 5 Stars In Euro NCAP Crash Tests
title: Bharat NCAP Safety Drama: Inside The Shocking Real-World Crash Test Of Indian Car
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Kia Seltos secures 90 per cent for post-crash safety and 84 per cent for occupant protection in the revised Euro NCAP crash tests The Kia Seltos has secured five stars in the 2026 Euro NCAP safety evaluation posting its highest category score in post-crash safety at 90 per cent. Crash protection stood at 84 per cent, followed by crash avoidance at 71 per cent and safe driving at 67 per cent. The organisation assessed a left-hand-drive Seltos 1.6T 6DCT 2WD weighing 1,490 kg. The verdict concerns the European test specification and does not establish an equivalent rating for the Indian version. The post-collision evaluation examined the assistance available to occupants and rescuers once an accident occurs. The SUV can brake automatically after an impact to reduce the chance of a second collision. Its emergency call function can transmit accident and occupant information to rescue personnel. The assessors awarded full scores for rescue documentation, hazard warning activation, and vehicle extrication provisions. Electrical safety measures relevant to emergency operations also underwent examination. The pedestrian assessment identified a substantial difference in injury protection between body regions. Pelvis protection received five per cent, compared to 85 per cent for the knee and tibia and 80 per cent for the femur. The head protection assessment scored 82 per cent for children and 63 per cent for adults. These measurements concern pedestrians struck by the vehicle and are separate from the injury readings recorded for passengers in the cabin. Safety Assessment Overall Score Individual Test Test Score Safe Driving 67% Driver Engagement 73% Crash Avoidance 71% Lane Departure 88% Crash Protection 84% Side Impact 96% Post Crash Safety 90% Vehicle Extrication 100% The frontal offset test produced marginal chest protection for the driver and a weak grade for the front passenger chest. Euro NCAP also examined the potential injury risk to another vehicle and found low collision aggressiveness. The separate full-width barrier impact returned good or adequate grades for the critical body regions of all assessed occupants. The results differed according to the collision configuration and seating position. The side movable barrier impact produced good protection for every critical region examined. The side pole collision presented a tougher scenario and returned a marginal grade for the driver chest. The centre airbag helped prevent contact between the two front occupants, and head protection was good. The rear impact tests revealed another contrast: the dynamic driver evaluation earned 97 per cent, but the static rear passenger evaluation received 38 per cent. The crash avoidance trials examined automatic emergency braking, lane assistance, and possible collisions at junctions. Frontal collision prevention earned 67 per cent and low-speed collision prevention returned 70 per cent. The SUV also warned occupants about cyclists approaching from behind before a door opened. The tests identified inconsistent responses to pedestrians and cyclists crossing its path at lower speeds. Driver acceptance of the lane assistance system nevertheless received full points. The safe driving evaluation checked seat belt warnings, driver attention monitoring, and recognition of road speed limits. The Seltos identified unfastened belts, rear occupants, unusual seating positions, fatigue, distraction, and mobile phone activity, but lacked an unattended-child alert. An extended road evaluation in France, Italy, and Spain measured speed limit identification over around 2,000 km. The system correctly identified limits in 87 per cent of instances accounting for 94 per cent of the travelled distance.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Gaadiwaadi.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

title: Production-Spec Hyundai Neira MPV (Rebadged Carens Clavis) Breaks Cover
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Hyundai Neira pre-bookings will begin in Indonesia on November 20 as the locally manufactured seven-seat electric MPV prepares for its official debut The Hyundai Neira will become available for pre-booking at GAIKINDO Auto Week 2026 in Indonesia – scheduled from November 20 to 29. The production-spec electric MPV follows the prototype presented at the Gaikindo Indonesia International Auto Show earlier this year. The rebadged Kia Carens Clavis will be manufactured locally there to save costs. The Indonesian electric car market offers considerable potential for the new model according to research conducted by Populix. The survey found that 74 per cent of millennial and Gen Z respondents expressed interest in purchasing an electric vehicle. Hyundai ranked among the automotive manufacturers considered by these prospective customers. The company also secured a 92 per cent aftersales satisfaction rating and a position among the top three brands in the same research. The Neira will become the first locally manufactured seven-seat electric SUV from Hyundai in Indonesia. The company has confirmed a high Domestic Component Level (TKDN) but the exact localisation percentage has not been announced. The MPV has a three-row cabin suitable for family transportation and an SUV-inspired design. The electric MPV will undertake a demonstration journey from Kilometer Nol in Banda Aceh to Banda Neira before its official market introduction. The starting point lies at the westernmost tip of Indonesia and the final destination is situated in the Banda Islands. The itinerary consists of mountainous stretches, winding roads, steep inclines and ferry crossings. Hyundai intends to assess the vehicle under varied geographical and weather conditions. The programme will also examine the practicality of long-distance electric travel in Indonesia. The manufacturer currently provides access to around 600 public charging points under agreements involving Charge Point Operators. Hyundai has established a target of more than 1,000 accessible charging points by 2027. The network serves electric vehicle owners travelling between different Indonesian cities. The company also recommends overnight battery replenishment at home via a dedicated wall charger. The Neira battery capacity and certified driving range have not been disclosed. Actual range will depend on driving habits, vehicle operating conditions and the selected drive mode. The dealership and service network in Indonesia currently consists of more than 100 outlets. The manufacturer has announced plans for 22 additional facilities before the end of 2026 including locations in Karawang, Makassar and Banjar. The expansion programme will improve access to maintenance and customer assistance in different regions. The myHyundaiCare programme provides supplementary services for electric vehicle owners in Indonesia. The Premium Courtesy Car facility offers temporary transportation for eligible customers whose vehicles require maintenance. Hyundai also provides 24-hour emergency assistance via its customer service centre or an SOS button. Other facilities consist of Roadside Assistance, Motorcycle Service, Take Me Home and Mobile Service.

raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - BMW is reportedly planning a ten-city Indian retail network as its first new 7 Series-based Alpina sedan approaches its international introduction BMW could bring Alpina to India in 2027 as it looks to create another tier of luxury cars between its own range and Rolls-Royce. Reuters reported that the German carmaker was examining a retail network in ten Indian cities. A recruitment notice concerning dealership selection and network planning provided further evidence of the preparations according to the report. The move comes amid a close contest in the domestic luxury car business. BMW sold 9,075 vehicles in the first half of 2026 with a 17 per cent annual rise as against 9,768 units for Mercedes-Benz which registered a 9 per cent increase. Mercedes-Maybach already serves customers seeking more individualised cars – a category where Alpina could compete without taking on the track-tuned character of BMW M. The German manufacturer intends to distinguish the marque using comfort, craftsmanship, high performance and personalisation. The first car in BMW’s new Alpina programme will be a 7 Series-based luxury sedan scheduled for international introduction in 2027. Reports suggest a return of the B7 name but BMW has not announced the production designation. The sedan will use a V8 engine retaining the type of powertrain historically associated with Alpina grand tourers. It has undergone high-speed evaluation at the Nardò Technical Center in Italy. The Alpina story began in Buchloe in 1965 when Burkard Bovensiepen created a business tuning BMW cars. Its work eventually progressed from engine modifications to complete automobiles with individual chassis calibration and cabin finishes. German authorities recognised Alpina as an automobile manufacturer in 1983. BMW bought the rights to the marque in 2022 while the previous independent vehicle programme ended in December 2025. In January 2026, BMW Alpina began operating as a distinct marque within BMW Group. The acquisition concerned the brand rights and not a purchase of the entire original company. Potential changes to import tariffs under the proposed India–European Union trade arrangement could influence the cost of selling these cars in India. The agreement’s provisions and implementation timetable still require confirmation, so reduced duties should not be treated as a certainty. Reuters noted that luxury vehicles made up just over one per cent of India’s 4.4 million passenger car sales in 2025. Questions concerning local prices, dealer locations, vehicle allocations and customer deliveries remain unanswered. The X7 is another BMW vehicle identified as a possible foundation for the revived marque. BMW engineering chief Joachim Post has spoken about both the flagship sedan and SUV as suitable starting points for future Alpina products. Separately, the Vision BMW Alpina concept unveiled in May 2026 previewed the new design identity. Its long grand touring body, four-seat interior and tailored materials illustrated the intended character of the marque. Engineering work at Nardò examined vehicle behaviour at speeds exceeding 300 kmph on the facility’s 12.6 km circuit. The car receives bespoke throttle calibration, transmission tuning, suspension revisions and aerodynamic changes intended to balance high-speed stability with relaxed motorway driving. Noise-reducing foam inside the tyres will help limit cabin sound. In addition, distinctive 20-spoke alloy wheels and four oval exhaust outlets preserve familiar Alpina design cues. Source

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

In real-world highway collisions, vehicles with unstable cabin architectures risk severe footwell intrusion, steering column collapse, and door jamming that traps occupants inside. Indian carmakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra have raised the bar by engineering 5-star crash resilience into their entry and mid-size platforms, compelling global competitors to rapidly upgrade their structural standards.

Our consumer verdict: never compromise on core structural integrity for cosmetic add-ons like ambient lighting or fancy touchscreens. raw_title: Tata Sierra EV Garners 5 Stars In Latest Round Of Bharat NCAP Crash Tests
title: Bharat NCAP Safety Drama: Inside The Shocking Real-World Crash Test Of Tata
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Tata Sierra EV has scored 30.62 points out of 32 for adult protection and 45 points out of 49 for child safety in latest Bharat NCAP safety tests The petrol and diesel versions of the Tata Sierra secured five stars in Bharat NCAP crash tests earlier this year. The electric model has now received the same adult and child occupant ratings as you might expect. The Sierra EV scored 30.62 points out of 32 for adult protection and 45 points out of 49 for child safety. The Bharat NCAP agency tested the Sierra EV Empowered A 75 QWD – the all-wheel-drive version carrying a 75 kWh battery. The assessment took place in June 2026 at a crash test weight of 2,412 kg. The five-star verdict also applies to the other versions in the official variant lineup. The tested dual e-motor SUV has a claimed MIDC driving range of 624 km. The frontal offset collision recorded good protection for the heads, chests, pelvises and thighs of both front occupants. The lower legs received adequate assessments and protection for the driver feet was marginal. The driver and passenger injury readings explain the deductions from the maximum score in this collision. The assessment simulates a partial frontal impact against a deformable barrier at 64 kmph. The Sierra EV received full points in the side movable barrier collision. The assessment recorded good protection for the head, chest, abdomen and pelvis. The separate side pole impact evaluation also returned an ‘Ok’ verdict. The barrier and pole procedures examine different collision situations. The pole assessment measures injuries caused by contact against a narrow fixed obstacle and its verdict contributes to the eligibility for the highest star rating. raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Hyundai Verna has attained scores of 28.22 points in adult occupant protection and 44 points in child occupant protection tests conducted by Bharat NCAP The Hyundai Verna earned five stars for adult and child occupant protection in Global NCAP tests in October 2023. The latest version of the midsize sedan has now secured the same star ratings under Bharat NCAP. The results assign 28.22 points out of 32 for adult safety and 44 points out of 49 for child safety protection tests. The crash tests took place in July 2026 and the agency selected the Verna HX 8 1.5 Turbo GDi DCT and HX 8 1.5 MPi iVT for evaluation. The published crash test prototype weighed 1,521 kg. The five star rating applies to the specified petrol manual and automatic variants from HX 2 to HX 10. The applicability identifies five MPi manual versions, four MPi iVT versions and three turbo petrol versions. The frontal offset deformable barrier assessment identified marginal protection for the driver and front passenger pelvis and thighs. The driver head and neck received good grades, but the chest, lower legs and feet were rated adequate. The front passenger received good ratings for the head, neck, chest and left shin. The right shin received an adequate assessment. The injury measurements explain the deductions in the frontal collision despite the five star adult classification. The evaluation involved a 64 kmph frontal impact. The side movable deformable barrier collision produced a better numerical result than the frontal assessment. The occupant head, abdomen and pelvis received good protection, and the chest was rated adequate. The separate side pole collision received an okay verdict. The assessment recorded good protection for the body regions evaluated in the pole collision. The two side tests examine different impact situations, and the pole verdict does not constitute another numerical component of the adult protection score. The child occupant evaluation involved rearward facing Joie i-Spin 360e restraints attached to the rear ISOFIX anchorages. The assessment examined an 18-month-old dummy and a three-year-old dummy. Both received full points in the frontal and side collisions. The child restraint installation evaluation also received full points. The remaining five point deduction came from the vehicle assessment category which examines child safety provisions apart from the injury readings recorded in the impact tests. The tested Verna variants had six airbags, electronic stability control, seat belt reminders, front pretensioners and load limiters. The sedan has ISOFIX anchorages for the outer rear seats, but the rear centre position lacks these mounting points. The standard safety equipment also comprises ABS, electronic brakeforce distribution, hill start assistance and rear parking sensors. Selected top-spec versions have Level 2 driver assistance features, front parking sensors and a 360-degree camera. The availability of these additional electronic systems varies by variant. The 2023 Global NCAP assessment awarded the earlier Verna 28.18 points out of 34 for adult protection and 42 out of 49 for child protection. The agency classified its bodyshell and footwell as unstable.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The electric motorcycle brand now operates in five Indian cities as its retail network grows following the C6 introduction earlier this year Royal Enfield has commenced Flying Flea operations in Kochi taking its electric motorcycle business into a fifth Indian city. The new retail network consists of a company-owned showroom and four authorised service facilities. The outlets will provide customers with access to the C6 motorcycle alongside technical assistance and routine maintenance. The Kochi introduction comes seven months after the brand began selling its first production electric motorcycle in April 2026. The retail programme initially commenced in Bengaluru before the brand established operations in Hyderabad, Pune and Chennai. Earlier network announcements specified twelve sales and service touchpoints in Bengaluru, ten in Pune and four in Hyderabad. The Chennai programme proposed fourteen locations comprising two company stores and twelve additional outlets associated with existing dealerships. The Chennai figure concerns the planned network and does not necessarily indicate that every facility has commenced operations. The Flying Flea C6 uses a 3.91 kWh lithium-ion battery offering an IDC-certified driving range of 154 km. The motorcycle has a claimed top speed of 115 kmph and weighs 124 kg. The front suspension employs a distinctive girder-style arrangement inspired by historic motorcycle construction. The electric roadster also features a compact silhouette, exposed structural elements, and a dedicated battery-powered architecture. The C6 is intended primarily for city commuting and shorter recreational journeys. The C6 is priced at Rs. 2.79 lakh when purchased outright. The Battery-as-a-Service option reduces the initial vehicle price to Rs. 1.99 lakh (both prices, ex-showroom) with separate subscription charges applicable for the battery. The motorcycle is offered in Storm Black, Flea Green and Parachute White colour schemes. The latter joined the original two paint options earlier this year. Owners also receive 24-hour roadside assistance under the manufacturer’s customer support programme. The electronic equipment comprises traction control, lean-angle-sensitive ABS, and a digital instrument interface. The motorcycle also supports Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and 4G connectivity for its connected vehicle functions. Flying Flea maintains a separate retail identity from Royal Enfield’s petrol motorcycle business with dedicated technical personnel assigned to electric vehicle servicing. The Kochi facilities will provide mechanical inspections, software-related assistance, and maintenance support for customers in the region. The commercial performance of the C6 remains relatively modest despite the growing retail network. Royal Enfield management revealed at its recent earnings discussion that around 200 motorcycles had been delivered in India since the commercial introduction. Owners had collectively travelled more than 1.25 lakh km at that point. The local operations have been accompanied by overseas introductions in Paris, Barcelona, Rome, Berlin and London. The five European cities received the C6 in 2026 as Flying Flea established its international retail business. The company has also showcased the scrambler-style S6 as its second electric motorcycle with commercial availability planned for 2027. The Flying Flea name originates from the lightweight Royal Enfield military motorcycle produced in the 1940s providing a historical connection for the manufacturer’s modern electric division.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Gaadiwaadi.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

Indian carmakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra have raised the bar by engineering 5-star crash resilience into their entry and mid-size platforms, compelling global competitors to rapidly upgrade their structural standards.

Our consumer verdict: never compromise on core structural integrity for cosmetic add-ons like ambient lighting or fancy touchscreens. Prioritize vehicles with certified 5-star Bharat NCAP or Global NCAP ratings, verified stable bodyshell integrity, and standard Electronic Stability Program (ESP) to ensure maximum survivability on unpredictable Indian roads.
